name: Copper Processing
description: Turn copper into machine parts and use mechanical power to improve ore yield.

pages.text: $(bold)From metal to machinery$()$(br2)The Copper Age starts by turning your first ingots into manufactured parts. The Primitive Anvil makes Copper Plates, and the Mechanical Grinder is the first machine that rewards building a working rotational network.

pages.title: Primitive Anvil
pages.text: Right-click the anvil with a Copper Ingot, then strike it four times with the Primitive Hammer. The workpiece is shown on the anvil and becomes a Copper Plate after the final strike.

$(bold)Copper Plates$()$(br2)Copper Plates reinforce many Copper Age mechanisms: control blocks, protection devices, the brake and the crank all build on this first metalworking step.$(br2)Use an empty hand on the completed anvil workpiece to pick it up.

pages.title: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: Place the Mechanical Grinder Base and put the Grinder Stone directly above it, then right-click the base to form the two-block machine.

pages.name: Mechanical Grinder
pages.text: The Grinder Stone sits directly above the base. Mechanical input is on the LEFT side of the stone base. Place a horizontal Wooden Shaft against the visible bearing. The grinder requires at least 20 mechanical speed and 4 torque.

$(bold)Crushing Chalcocite$()$(br2)Right-click the formed grinder with Chalcocite Ore. With at least 20 speed and 4 torque it runs for about eight seconds and produces Crushed Chalcocite.$(br2)If the drivetrain stops, processing pauses rather than losing progress. Use an empty hand to retrieve output.

$(bold)Why crush it?$()$(br2)Direct Primitive Furnace processing remains valid: one Chalcocite Ore gives one Copper Ingot plus Slag.$(br2)Crushing first improves the same furnace batch to $(bold)two Copper Ingots$() plus Slag. Your mechanical workshop therefore improves resource efficiency instead of existing only as a progression lock.

pages.title: Ore Washer Controller
pages.text: The crafted block is the controller, not the whole machine. The Washer is a 3x2x3 JSON multiblock. It also needs one Mechanical Input Bearing so Gear V2 can enter the formed structure.

pages.title: Washer I/O Ports
pages.text: The Washer now has real automation ports. The tall rear port is INPUT only and forwards into the washer's recipe slot. The low front port is OUTPUT only and exposes both concentrate and byproduct slots for extraction.

pages.name: Mechanical Ore Washer
pages.text: The book now matches the real structure coordinates. Relative to the controller: Item Input is REAR, Item Output is FRONT, Clean Fluid Input is LEFT, Dirty Fluid Output is RIGHT, and the Mechanical Input Bearing sits directly ABOVE the Item Output. The Visualize button uses this exact arrangement.

pages.title: Fluid I/O + Pipes
pages.text: The Washer has separate fluid ports. Feed clean water into the green-marked Fluid Input. Dirty process water leaves through the brown-marked Fluid Output. Copper Fluid Pipes are passive transport blocks; connect the output line to a Copper Fluid Tank to collect Dirty Water.

pages.title: Mechanical Water Pump
pages.text: Place the pump directly above a water source. Its TOP is the only fluid output. Place the pump against the end of a Wooden Shaft: the visible crank-wheel side is the only mechanical input, and power does not pass through the opposite side. It needs at least 15 RPM and 2 torque. Faster rotation increases flow up to 200 mB/t.

pages.title: Copper Fluid Tank
pages.text: The Copper Fluid Tank stores 8000 mB of one fluid. Connect a Copper Fluid Pipe to the TOP socket. The tank periodically pulls from reachable multiblock Fluid Outputs, so Dirty Water from the Ore Washer can be collected without making every pipe tick. The four inspection windows show the real fluid texture, color and fill level.

pages.title: Mechanical Transfer Arm
pages.text: Early item automation stays physical. The control console is the block's FRONT/FACING side and naturally faces the player after placement. Its F/B/L/R buttons show orange IN for the source and blue OUT for the destination, and Left/Right match the visible buttons from the panel view.

$(bold)Arm filters$()$(br2)The lower window on the FRONT console is the filter slot. Right-click it with an item to set a ghost filter; the item is not consumed. The panel shows ANY with no filter, ALLOW for whitelist, or BLOCK for blacklist. Empty-hand click toggles ALLOW/BLOCK; sneak-right-click clears it.$(br2)If the destination fills, the arm waits with the item in its claw instead of deleting it.

$(bold)Washer operation$()$(br2)Feed crushed ore through the rear Item Input. The Washer stores 4000 mB of clean water and 4000 mB of Dirty Water. Each cassiterite batch consumes 250 mB clean water and produces 250 mB Dirty Water. Connect the Dirty Fluid Output to a Copper Fluid Tank; otherwise the Washer eventually pauses when its internal waste tank fills.$(br2)Dirty Water is intended for later treatment/recycling rather than permanent disposal.

pages.title: Sifter Controller
pages.text: The Sifter is also a structure rather than a one-block machine. Build the 3x2x2 frame and form it from the controller. It uses the same Item Input and Item Output modules as the Washer, while its reciprocating drive still comes from a Wooden Crank placed directly behind the controller.

pages.name: Mechanical Sifter
pages.text: Build the frame exactly as shown and right-click the controller to form it. Viewed from the controller/front side, Item Input is the left front corner and Item Output is the right front corner. Put a Wooden Crank directly behind the controller with its rod output pointing into the low copper slide bearing. The lower and upper screens move opposite each other to classify material.

$(bold)Cassiterite -> Tin$()$(br2)Cassiterite now has the first complete beneficiation chain: $(br)1. Mechanical Grinder -> Crushed Cassiterite$(br)2. Ore Washer + water -> Washed Cassiterite$(br)3. Crank-driven Sifter -> Tin Concentrate$(br)4. Primitive Furnace + coal -> Tin Ingot$(br2)The Cassiterite sifting recipe needs at least 15 speed and 2 torque, runs for about eight seconds, and has a 15% chance to produce Flint as a byproduct.

$(bold)First Bronze$()$(br2)Combine three Copper Ingots with one Tin Ingot to prepare a Bronze Alloy Charge. Fire the charge with coal in the Primitive Furnace to produce four Bronze Ingots.$(br2)Making the first Bronze therefore proves that the Copper workshop can mine, crush, wash, classify and smelt an alloy feedstock.

$(bold)Data-driven ore processing$()$(br2)Grinding, washing and sifting requirements now live in recipe JSON instead of being hard-coded into each machine. New minerals can define their own speed, torque, time, outputs and byproduct chance without another Java machine class.$(br2)This is the foundation for processing the rest of Magneticraft2's ore catalogue through later ages.
